title: Pruning and Attribution — Observability Weeknote
body:
Weekly handoff notes from Observability — focus this week: trace/span pruning, dashboard ROI, and cost attribution experiments. Lightweight capture for the team; please edit inline if you own an action.

Meeting: Observability sync (Mon 2027-04-05, 10:00–10:45) — ad-hoc follow-up captured on 2027-04-06.
Attendees: Priya N., Ethan C., Marta R., Devon B., Anika S., (drop-in) Kofi M.
Absentees: none flagged.

TL;DR
- We greenlit a small, staged experiment to prune low-value spans from our central trace pipeline to cut trace storage by ~18% while preserving tail-latency attribution.
- Dashboard pruning: retire 9 panels and consolidate 3 dashboards into a single "Model-cost-attribution" dashboard to reduce noise for on-call.
- Cost telemetry: prototype attribution by model family (open-llama/llm-x) using sampling-weighted token counts; early numbers suggest a 12% discrepancy compared to naive token-based billing due to batching/kv-cache effects.

Notes and context
1) Trace/span pruning experiment (Ethan lead)
   - Problem: high-cardinality internal spans from signal adapters (trace-source-filter) account for ~40% of raw span count and low signal for latency/cost debugging. Storage and ingestion costs rising.
   - Proposal: implement a two-tier pruning policy in the ingest pipeline:
       * Tier A (full retention): spans with tags {error=true} OR route=/generate OR duration>50ms -> keep full context.
       * Tier B (light retention): spans from adapters, healthchecks, and model-ops heartbeats -> keep metadata only (service, span_name, start_ts, duration_bucket).
       * Sampling fallback: during ~peak windows (>80% ingestion throughput), downsample Tier B further to 1/10.
   - Metrics to track during trial: span count delta, storage bytes/day, number of incidents where pruned spans were required for root cause analysis (want zero for Tier A), weekly cost delta.
   - Rollout plan: 2-week canary on staging -> 1-week shadow on prod ingestion (no pruning, just tagging results) -> gradual apply across regions.
   - Risks/mitigations: accidental pruning of useful spans; mitigation: quick revert via feature flag and preserve 48h full-window occasionally for random 1% requests.

2) Dashboard consolidation and pruning (Marta + Anika)
   - Current state: ~27 dashboards flagged as "on-call", many panels duplicate across teams. On-call noise rising.
   - Actions decided:
       * Retire panels that haven't been viewed in 30 days and have <5 correlated incidents in 90 days (automated query by Marta). Expected retire count: 9.
       * Consolidate model-cost-* (3 dashboards) into a single view with an explainer panel on attribution methodology (pull from Confluence).
       * Add a small "quick pulse" panel to the SRE overview showing 99.9th token latency by model family (1m resolution) so front-line can triage regressions faster.
   - Ownership: Marta to run the retire script (OBS-4921), Anika to design the consolidated layout and micro-copy.

3) Cost telemetry and model attribution (Priya + Devon)
   - Problem: our billing-aligned cost attribution is off when we compare it to token-metering in downstream teams because of batching and KV cache hits. Teams ask for per-model cost slices that match invoiced numbers.
   - Experiment design:
       * Collect sampling-weighted token counts from the router (tokens_emitted + tokens_served_from_cache) with batch-size histogram.
       * Use model-family mapping and GPU runtime metrics to estimate per-request GPU-seconds, then multiply by per-hour GPU price to derive a per-request cost.
       * Validate: sample 10k requests from last week and compare aggregated per-model cost to invoiced usage.
   - Preliminary result: naive token-share method overallocates cost to smaller models by ~12%. Hypothesis: larger models benefit more from batching and longer KV-cache reuse, causing lower per-token GPU-s cost.
   - Next step: Devon will produce a short reproducible notebook and push to PR (#314).

4) Tracing sampling policy v2 (technical decision)
   - We decided against uniform head-based sampling. Instead adopt adaptive sampling: higher retention for error/slow traces and for routes tagged as "sensitive" for rollouts.
   - Implementation notes: sampling policy runs in router before enrichment to minimize wasted enrichment cost. Policy config stored in ConfigService (JSON blob) and versioned.

Action items (owner — ETA)
- Ethan: implement Tier A/B pruning prototype in staging ingest (OBS-4921) — staging canary by 2027-04-12.
- Marta: run dashboard retire query and list panels for removal; coordinate with owners to archive by 2027-04-09.
- Anika: design consolidated Model-cost dashboard mock and micro-copy draft — due 2027-04-11.
- Devon: finish reproducible notebook for cost attribution and open PR -> https://github.com/redwood-inference/observability/pull/314 — due 2027-04-08.
- Priya: update Confluence explainer for sampling/playbook with new Tier definitions — update by 2027-04-10.
- SRE on-call: watch for regressions after pruning shadow week; escalate via #observability-alerts.

Open questions / unresolved
- How long should we keep the metadata-only Tier B spans (48h vs 7d)? Shorter retention reduces cost but may hurt mid-term incident investigation. Suggest 72h as a compromise for the canary.
- For cost attribution, do we include preemptible GPU discounts and spot evictions in model-level cost? (Finance wants them included but needs mapping). Action: Priya to sync with Finance on discount mapping and add to notebook assumptions.
- Is the 1/10 downsample multiplier for Tier B during peaks aggressive enough? Ethan to calibrate using historical peak windows.

Incidents / recent findings
- Small regression (non-prod) where a misconfigured router policy caused 0.2% of traces to lose model_name tag; traced to a downstream enrichment race. Fix: reorder enrichment call (PR merged by Kofi).
- Dashboard performance: heavy queries on Model-cost dashboards causing spikes in Grafana CPU during business hours; mitigation: add plexi caches (1m TTL) and reduce panel refresh to 30s.

Misc notes (brainstormed)
- Idea: "trace-compact" microformat — store a compressed, tokenized stack for certain classes of spans to allow reconstructing context when needed without high cardinality retention. Prototype later Q2.
- Consider a monthly "dashboard audit" where owners must re-confirm panels or they get auto-archived. Could be implemented as a small internal app.

Quick links / references
- Playbook draft: confluence:Trace-Sampling-Playbook-v2
- Jira: OBS-4921 (span pruning experiment)
- PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/observability/pull/314 (cost-attribution notebook)

If you own any action, please add ETA and escalate blockers to #observability-eng. We'll reconvene next Monday for canary readout.

-- Priya
